beats.story: After a lunchtime spent eating a ham sammy while solo people-watching at Prince's Island Park, clashing with the crowds of laughing families, ball- busting businessmen, and brightly colored runners, I return and confirm that Rhonda has officially shared my half of the inventory data grid with me, even though Caitlin received her piece yesterday evening. No matter, because I already finished it. Now I just have to wait a believable amount of time to return it. Caitlin is throwing a plastic container, half full of browning Caesar salad, into the waste bin under her desk. Typical. There's a whole recycling center in the lunchroom, yet she chooses to leave it up to the members of the cleaning service to properly dispose of her mess. I log in to check if Caitlin's already returned her part of the grid. Instead, I find another email from Cliff asking to schedule a meeting.
beats.story_cn: 午饭时间我独自在王子岛公园啃着火腿三明治看人来人往——与那些笑闹的家庭、拼命三郎的商务人士、色彩鲜艳的跑者们格格不入。回到公司发现朗达果然已经把半份数据清单发给我了，而凯特琳昨晚就收到了她的那份。无所谓，反正我早就做完了。现在只需等个合理的时间再提交。凯特琳正把半盒发黄的凯撒沙拉扔进桌下垃圾桶。典型做派。茶水间明明有整套回收站，她偏要等清洁工来处理她制造的垃圾。我登录系统想看凯特琳是否提交了，却瞥见克利夫新邮件：要求安排会议。

beats.story: Three dots bounce across the screen as Caitlin types. I lean in, my skin cooling, the goose bumps on the back of my wrist matching the ones continuously dancing on the screen. Before any message appears, the accessible door beeps open, followed by a sleek stroller. "Helloooo!" calls the stroller pusher, also known as Celeste Laird, who is supposed to be on maternity leave for another six months. And unless that baby knows how to file, she must be bringing it to meet us. Caitlin and Garret both instantly rise from their seats, leaving me in the dark. The office is a blur of oohs and bright, tender faces, all rushing toward Celeste. I also notice a few stragglers, like Joy and Armin, who are hiding the screen guard and wrist support they each respectively looted from her desk as soon as she'd left.
beats.story_cn: 聊天框里三个点还在跳动，凯特琳正在输入。我俯身向前，皮肤发凉，腕后的鸡皮疙瘩与屏幕上持续跳动的点阵遥相呼应。消息尚未弹出，无障碍门“嘀”地开了，一辆时髦婴儿车率先入画。“来啦——！”推车人——本该还有六个月产假的塞莱斯特·莱尔德朗声招呼。除非这娃娃会自己整理文件，否则她准是来带孩子见同事的。凯特琳和加勒特瞬间弹起，只剩我呆坐原地。办公室顿时淹没在“噢噢啊啊”的赞叹与柔光满面的笑容里，所有人涌向塞莱斯特。我也瞥见几个掉队者，比如乔伊和阿明，正手忙脚乱地遮掩从塞莱斯特桌上顺走的屏幕挡板和腕托——就在她离开的瞬间抢的。

beats.story: I sit frozen, still staring at my screen. The three dots in the chat have disappeared. I was so close to knowing exactly what she had in store. Why can't we normalize telling babies and the people who love them to fuck off in some polite way? Rhonda leans over my cubicle wall and says, "Celeste brought her little guy in, isn't that sweet?" She stares pointedly from me to the group of baby fans in case I've lost all six of my senses. Caitlin's already at the stroller, front and center. I smile stiffly but make no move to stand and join them. Then Gregory stomps out of his office, coffee in hand, rocking his chino fucking pants, and nods directly at me.
beats.story_cn: 我僵坐着，仍瞪着屏幕。聊天框的三点提示消失了。我本可以知道她究竟盘算什么。为什么我们不能发明种体面的方式，叫那些抱着孩子来打扰工作的人滚蛋？朗达探过隔板墙：“塞莱斯特带宝宝来了，真可爱对吧？”她目光灼灼地在我和那群“婴儿崇拜者”间扫视，仿佛我六感尽失。凯特琳早已挤到婴儿车正前方。我扯出僵硬的微笑却不起身加入。这时格雷戈里端着咖啡从办公室重重踱出，晃着他那该死的卡其裤，朝我径直点头。

beats.story: "Let's go see the baby!" And it's certain: not looking at this little asshole will cost me something. So much of what I do here has nothing to do with my actual job, yet these little interactions matter so much. I trudge out of my seat and make my way toward the shit show. As soon as I reach the coffee-breathed group of people, I lock eyes with the baby and it, predictably, begins to wail. Celeste picks it up and pats it on the back to soothe it while people continue to ask her boring questions about motherhood, her sleep schedule, and laundry. This little human doesn't even realize the greatness of this: the only time in your life when people will simply ignore your public outbursts. The rest of us must cry without actually crying. This child, I learn as Celeste continues to soothe it, is named Thomas.
beats.story_cn: “去看看小宝宝吧！”躲是躲不掉了：不瞧这小屁孩一眼，准得付出点代价。我在这儿干的事儿，多半和本职工作八竿子打不着，可这些细枝末节的交锋偏偏要紧得很。我蹒跚着走向这场闹剧，刚凑近那群浑身咖啡味的人堆，便和那婴儿四目相对。果然，小东西张嘴就嚎。塞莱斯特把它抱起来拍背安抚，旁人则继续围着她，用乏味的问题轰炸她：当妈的感觉如何？睡眠规律吗？衣服谁洗？这小人类压根不明白自己正处在何等黄金时代：这辈子唯一能理直气壮当众撒泼的时光。咱们这些成年人，连哭都得憋着。从塞莱斯特哄孩子的间隙，我得知这小家伙叫托马斯。

beats.story: I watch his little eyes dart around the room, taking it all in. Maybe Thomas is just now realizing that eventually he will grow up to spend all his daylight hours under fluorescent lights and water-stained ceiling tiles. I don't mean to chuckle at that depressing thought, and I stifle it as soon as I can, but that doesn't stop a few eyes from drawing my way while I pretend I didn't just cackle at a technically crying baby. Then Thomas begins being passed around like a hot burrito. I curl my hands close against my chest and try to back away. When Caitlin takes said bundle, it stops crying in an instant, and her face softens in a way that makes me realize how hard it's been lately. She inhales the top of the baby's head -- which is a choice -- then smiles and says to Celeste, "So how is being a mom?" Celeste starts describing things that sound dire as shit. Rhonda, who has taken up a position behind Celeste's left shoulder, nods along while intermittently agreeing or interjecting about how it was with her sweet baby Carl.
beats.story_cn: 我瞧着那对小眼珠滴溜溜地转，把周遭一切尽收眼底。或许托马斯这才意识到，自己终将长大，在冷光灯管和水渍斑驳的天花板瓷砖下耗尽每一个白昼。这念头着实悲凉，我差点笑出声来，连忙硬生生憋住，却仍有几道目光循声瞟来，而我只能装作刚才没对着一个理论上正在哭的婴儿发出嗤笑。接着，托马斯开始了他如滚烫墨西哥卷饼般的传递之旅。我双手蜷缩在胸前，试图悄悄后撤。轮到凯特琳接过那团襁褓时，哭声戛然而止，她脸上的线条瞬间柔和下来，那神情让我窥见她近来过得有多艰难。她深深吸了吸婴儿头顶——这品味可真独特——然后对塞莱斯特笑道：“当妈感觉怎么样？”塞莱斯特开始描述种种听来惨不忍睹的境况。不知何时已站到塞莱斯特左肩后方的罗娜，一边附和着点头，一边时不时插话，絮叨她那乖宝宝卡尔当年如何如何。

beats.story: Gregory randomly pokes the fucking baby in the belly, and the cries start again in a screeching pitch. Has anyone ever punched him in the face? "How was the birth?" Stu for some cursed reason has to ask. I take a step back in order to avoid sticking around for Celeste's answer. Rhonda flashes me a disapproving stare. Why is it so socially acceptable to discuss a human getting pushed or cut out of a body, yet somehow, it's unprofessional for me to simply work rather than hold the tiny person I don't even know, while it's wearing something designed to catch any fecal matter that comes out of it? I quietly take another step away. And another.
beats.story_cn: 格里高利随手捅了捅那该死的婴儿的肚子，尖利的啼哭声再度炸开。有人揍过他的脸吗？“生孩子顺利吗？”斯图鬼知道抽了什么风，非得问这个。我后退一步，免得被迫留下来听塞莱斯特的回答。罗娜朝我甩来一个谴责的眼神。为什么讨论一个人从身体里被挤出来或剖出来就如此正当合宜，而我只是想工作、不想抱这个我压根不认识、还穿着设计来兜屎兜的小东西，反倒显得不专业了？我又悄悄后退一步。再退一步。

beats.story: I pass Joey and am almost in the clear when Caitlin loudly says, "Don't take that personally -- it's her. We need to catch up about that as well." I lower into my chair, and her fractured message chain greets me on my screen. Who does she think she is? Her cackle rattles with the flash of the burning-out fluorescent above her. It's the cackle of someone who believes herself a goddess. And that's it! I check to make sure nobody is around, and thankfully, they're all still at the infant show. I flip to her document folder and type Iamagoddess19* when prompted.
beats.story_cn: 我经过乔伊身边，眼看就要溜之大吉，凯特琳却扬高嗓门道：“别往心里去——她是对我来的。我们俩也得聊聊那档子事。”我跌坐回椅子，屏幕上跳出来的是她那支离破碎的信息链。她当自己是谁？她的笑声在头顶那盏濒临熄灭的日光灯的闪烁中哗啦作响，宛如一位自封女神的得意尖笑。就是它了！我迅速确认四下无人，谢天谢地，所有人都还在围观那个婴儿秀。我切换到她的文档文件夹，在提示框里敲下“我是个女神19*”。

options.fullOutcomeStory: An impulsive burst of stress led to a bizarre remark that echoed through the quiet office. You immediately regretted speaking without filtering.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 压力瞬间爆发，一句突兀的怪话在寂静的办公室里回荡。你立刻后悔了这未经滤过的失言。

beats.story: I try to stop myself from shaking as my heart pounds into my eardrums. I click, and in an instant her inventory report covers my screen. It's almost complete. I move a decimal, such a tiny thing. I change a 63 to 64, an easy typo to make if one's not focusing. My finger hesitates before clicking. I can't actually sabotage -- it's a different line. Deniability, even to myself, won't be an option.
beats.story_cn: 我强忍着颤抖，心跳如擂鼓般撞击耳膜。点击瞬间，她的库存报告铺满屏幕。几乎完整无缺。我移动一个小数点——如此微小的动作。将63改成64，走神时极易犯下的笔误。指尖在点击前迟疑。我无法真正破坏——那是另一行数据。连自欺欺人的余地都不会有。

beats.story: But as she passes the baby to Garret, I realize there's no telling what she's going to say to manipulate Cliff tomorrow. And there's no telling what else she's done over the years -- how much my reputation has been messed with in silent conversations and quiet sabotage. This is the only thing I can control. I save the changes and close out.
beats.story_cn: 但当她把婴儿递给加勒特时，我意识到无法预料她明天会用什么话术操纵克利夫。更无法预料这些年她还做过什么——我的名声在多少次窃窃私语与无声破坏中被侵蚀殆尽。这是我唯一能掌控的事。我保存修改，关闭页面。
